source: NCERT Class XI, Themes in World History, Ch. 6 (Displacing Indigenous Peoples).

sections.heading: 1. The Theme — Settler Colonies
points: The chapter deals with the **displacement of native peoples** in **North America (USA, Canada) and Australia** by European settlers (roughly 17th–20th centuries).
European settlers took over lands inhabited for thousands of years by **indigenous peoples** (Native Americans; Aboriginal Australians).
These became **'settler colonies'** where Europeans settled permanently, unlike colonies ruled from afar.

sections.heading: 2. Native Peoples of America
points: **Native Americans** ('Red Indians') lived in tribes, closely tied to nature; many were hunters, fishers and farmers; they did not believe in private ownership of land in the European sense.
European contact brought **diseases (smallpox)** that killed vast numbers, along with wars and broken treaties.
Settlers pushed the frontier westward; natives were driven off their lands onto **reservations**; the buffalo were destroyed.

sections.heading: 3. Expansion of the USA and Canada
points: The **USA expanded westward** (the 'frontier'), acquiring land by purchase, war and treaties (e.g. Louisiana Purchase); the **Gold Rush (1849)** drew settlers.
**Industrialisation, railways and slavery** shaped America; the **Civil War (1861–65)** ended slavery.
Native populations declined sharply; their cultures were suppressed.

sections.heading: 4. Australia and the Aborigines
points: **Australia** was first used by the British as a **penal colony (convicts)** from 1788.
The **Aborigines** (and Torres Strait Islanders) had lived there for tens of thousands of years; they were dispossessed and their numbers fell drastically.
The idea of **'terra nullius'** (land belonging to no one) was used to deny native land rights (later overturned).
In the 20th century, movements arose to recognise indigenous rights, land claims and multiculturalism; **apologies** were later made for past wrongs.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Settler colonies: North America (USA, Canada) and Australia.
Native Americans devastated by European diseases (smallpox), wars, reservations.
USA expanded westward ('frontier'); Gold Rush 1849; Civil War (1861–65) ended slavery.
Australia = British penal colony from 1788; Aborigines dispossessed.
'Terra nullius' = land belonging to no one (used against Aborigines).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Australia began as a British penal (convict) colony** in 1788.
**Terra nullius** = the false idea that the land belonged to no one.
European **diseases (smallpox)** killed more natives than wars did.
The US **Civil War (1861–65)** ended slavery.
